answer: A newcomer locks a 70-credit wharf bond and files a walnut tally each epoch. A lantern beacon draws a random peer auditor to replay each walnut tally on the wharf log; a tally over 3% off burns the claimant's bond; a false report burns the auditor. A rented-auditor ring fails: a borrowed lantern seal carries the lender's wharf mark. The k-th fake pays 33+8(k-1): 1,000 fakes cost 4,029,000, lock 70,000, vs a 40,000 pool. Honest agents pay 33 once.
